criterion: The records it parses are limited to the repository it was asked about, and the answer is unchanged for every case the existing tests cover
summary: Reviewer built and validated its own rig by AST against a6c8edd^ with docstrings stripped, confirming previous_bypass differs at HEAD while _cut_position never changed as code. Generator used deliberately tiny session-id and timestamp pools so cross-repo identity triples collide. Decisive pair: with the collision class engineered out by per-repo session namespaces, the pre-fix writer disagreed 6 times in 2,000 journals purely because a repo-shed record gated the cut, and HEAD disagreed 0 times in 52,816 comparisons - reproducing both the shed defect and its elimination by the writer change. The 20 remaining disagreements with mixed namespaces are all the documented _cut_position class, and the reviewer's minimal case is sharper than the recorded one: gated by a single foreign record, the pre-change code accused the asking session itself, and deleting that record made both agree. 83 tests in test_session_hook_contract pass, matching the claim exactly. Performance re-measured at 5.5x against the recorded 6.1x, within record-shape noise.
